display.purpose: Homepage hero; --text-display, normal-weight Archivo with an 80px desktop ceiling and component-specific responsive overrides. English hero uses 1.04 line height and a 0.8em secondary line.

headline.purpose: Public identity and section headings; --text-headline, 60px ceiling. Line heights vary from 1 to 1.1; token uses the retained ownership heading's 1.04, while English marketing headings use 1.06.

dashboard.purpose: Owner and visitor greetings; --text-dashboard, 48px ceiling, 32px on mobile. The public introduction also uses a related 48px tier.

title.purpose: --text-title, 24px reading-panel and capability headings; normal weight.

body.purpose: --text-body, 18px with 1.5 line height; public supporting copy and illustrative hero bubbles.

control.purpose: --text-control, 16px. Buttons use 500/1.2; navigation and ordinary message text use 400, messages with 1.5 line height.

small.purpose: --text-small, 14px supporting text and mobile message text; generally 1.5 line height.

caption.purpose: --text-caption, 12px message captions, notices and prompt labels; 1.25 in the demo chip, otherwise inherited 1.5.

shadows.name: illustrative-bubble
shadows.purpose: Retained illustrative story-bubble CSS; the current homepage does not render these bubbles. Ordinary chat messages remain flat.

focus.name: keyboard
focus.purpose: Focus-visible anchors, buttons, inputs, textareas, selects, summaries and explicitly focusable elements.

focus.name: compound-url-input
focus.purpose: URL input within its rounded compound wrapper; retains the same outline color and width.

focus.name: ownership-and-footer
focus.purpose: Ownership links, buttons, selects and summaries, plus footer links, buttons and summaries, use the existing signal-light shade on their dark planes. Source scopes: .ownership-section :where(a, button, select, summary):focus-visible and .site-footer :where(a, button, summary):focus-visible.

focus.name: billing-option
focus.purpose: Drawn on the enclosing label when its native radio is focus-visible; the transparent input's own outline is suppressed.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Native easing token: cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), used for link indicators, button icons and illustrative reply arrival.

motion.name: control-color
motion.purpose: Button background-color, color and border-color transitions.

motion.name: control-icon
motion.purpose: Standard button icon translates 3px horizontally on enabled hover.

motion.name: navigation-indicator
motion.purpose: Public link underline grows horizontally on hover and current page.

motion.name: illustrative-reply
motion.purpose: Retained story-reply CSS arrives from translateY(14px) with a clipped lower edge, only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. The current homepage does not render this reply.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disable transitions and smooth scrolling. Reply animation is already gated to no-preference.

themeAffordances.darkMode: Contextual light/dark panels; no separate automatic dark-mode theme.

tonalRamps.method: Synthesized OKLCH swatch ramps, dark to light, eight lightness steps from 15% to 95%, retaining each source color's approximate hue and chroma. CSS gamut mapping applies to out-of-gamut swatches.
tonalRamps.purpose: Panel metadata only. Canonical hex values remain the shipping authority; these ramps are not additional CSS tokens.

source.literalAccent: signal-light is #FF6ABA in dark ownership headings and copy, runtime-link hover, ownership/footer control focus, the history destination icon and Patrick invitation; no --signal-light variable exists.
source.runtimeTruth: Interactive local/demo prototypes; role selection is simulated, responses are predefined, and URLs are not crawled.
source.language: src/app/page.tsx wraps the English homepage in lang=en; src/components/site-shell.tsx supplies English shell copy. The public Collaborator and both dashboards remain French.
source.preferenceFlow: src/components/ownership-options.tsx supplies native hosting/intelligence selects; src/components/collaborator-pricing.tsx supplies native monthly/annual radios. Both update shared in-page preferences in src/components/collaborator-offer-context.tsx. Its EncounterLink merges explicit link defaults with shared choices, with user-selected values taking precedence, so every homepage encounter CTA preserves the combined selection. src/components/meet-collaborator.tsx shows the received preferences in a pink-wash definition list. src/lib/collaborator-offer.ts owns allowlisted values, encounter links and price labels; PRODUCT.md owns the intended offer. No provisioning, connection or payment occurs; history import and Hermes integration remain planned.
source.routeMetadata: Route pages retain server-owned metadata; src/app/page.tsx composes the client CollaboratorOfferProvider around its homepage content and shared shell.
source.footerDisclosures: src/components/site-shell.tsx uses native details/summary for English preview privacy and terms. Dark-plane hairline rows, muted body copy, signal-light keyboard outlines and a plus rotated 45 degrees when open; two columns stack at 699px.
source.illustration: public/images/working-together.jpg; Unsplash source in public/images/SOURCES.md, embedded provenance and a visible illustration credit. Desktop photographic overlay; mobile in-flow 210px crop below the CTA.
source.encounterResult: Successful submission focuses the response heading and scrolls it into view; instant for reduced motion, smooth otherwise. Errors remain at the form.

narrative.overview:
The user-selected reference is whatsapp.com: warm cream, near-black ink, normal-weight sans-serif headings, photographic panels, pill controls and conversational bubbles. Fuchsia replaces its green. The visual authority is the implemented `src/app/globals.css`, with Archivo loaded in `src/app/layout.tsx`; this specification replaces the former serif, public-single-page system.

One reusable family supports four distinct surfaces: `/` (homepage), `/@patrick-chassany` (public AI Collaborator), `/dashboard/patrick` (owner demo) and `/dashboard/visiteur` (visitor demo). The homepage is English; the public Collaborator and both dashboards remain French, with language-aware shared shell components. Public pages use expressive scale; role-specific dashboards use smaller, functional hierarchy and standard list/detail organization. These routes are implemented prototypes: role selection, responses, work and URL previews are simulated or local, with no real login, AI execution or crawl implied. Surface composition belongs in `.impeccable/surfaces/`.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream and dark tonal planes, with hairline separation.
Archivo throughout; large public headings and compact operational hierarchy.
Fuchsia actions, contextual accent text and pink selections.
Pill controls, generous panels and recognizable message silhouettes.
Visible demo labels and local illustrative photography.

rules.name: The Contextual Accent Rule
rules.body: Use signal for solid actions, signal-deep for accent text on cream, and signal-light for accent text on dark. Pink wash carries selection without making every item a solid action.

rules.name: The Functional Scale Rule
rules.body: Carry the same sans-serif identity into dashboards, using the dashboard and title tiers instead of public hero scale. Keep ordinary prose at weight 400, and use size, spacing and position to establish hierarchy.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Establish depth with surface contrast and hairlines. Reserve shadows for illustrative message bubbles and the account dropdown.

dos: Do use the WhatsApp-derived cream, sans-serif, pill-control and conversational family consistently across all four surfaces.
Do preserve the smaller functional hierarchy and distinct owner/visitor navigation in dashboards.
Do use contextual fuchsia shades, pink wash, white panels and hairlines according to their roles.
Do keep keyboard focus visible and honor reduced motion.
Do label simulated responses, activity, validation and URL previews visibly; keep knowledge distinct from memory and use AI Collaborator terminology.
Do retain local illustrative assets, source records and embedded provenance without presenting them as real people or product evidence.
donts: Don't restore the obsolete serif, single-column-only, white-ban or one-fuchsia-element constraints.
Don't add shadows to ordinary controls, chat messages or reading panels.
Don't describe demo role selection as real login, local previews as crawling or deployment, or predefined answers as live AI work.
Don't rename Patrick's AI Collaborator to Pacha or present owner sections as the four application surfaces.
